narrative:
The model estimated a 68.8% chance that you would fail the bar exam on the first try. Because your law school admission was tied to that prediction, the application was rejected: the model judged the risk high enough to deny admission, not that success is impossible.

The strongest factor driving this prediction was your third-year class decile. Your 3rd-decile standing was below the accepted-student average near 5.8, and it pushed the prediction toward bar-exam failure. The second strongest factor was your first-year class decile: your 4th-decile standing, compared with an accepted average near 6.0, also pushed toward failure. Third was your family income bracket; your upper-middle background contributed toward failure, though it ranked behind the two academic indicators.

To move forward, ask admissions for individualized feedback and, if available, a human review of your file. Ask what academic thresholds would make your application competitive, strengthen your record through additional relevant coursework, and consider retaking the LSAT if permitted. Reapply only after you can show improved evidence, and provide context explaining any circumstances behind your class standing.
